subject: LuminaHealth: Throughput & Error Surge — Executive Coordination
messages:
From: Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@luminahq.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike in 5xx + tokens delayed across /generate endpoint

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 500s and long tail token delays across our production traffic hitting /v1/generate at ~07:45 PST. Throughput has dropped to roughly 20% of normal for a subset of requests (mostly long-chat sessions). We attached a sample error screenshot and a short heap of telemetry from our side. This is impacting our triage workflows and some scheduled batch jobs.

Can someone escalate? We are under an SLO and this is user-facing.

Attached: lumina_error_snapshot.png (screenshot)

Thanks,
Sam
Samantha Nguyen
Director, Platform Engineering
LuminaHealth

Team — forwarding LuminaHealth. Short: large throughput drop + increased 5xx rate. They’re a mid-enterprise Dedicated customer on a reserved pool (RDW-3241-LH). Need an initial triage and an exec-facing status for Sam in 30m.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you confirm whether the dedicated pool for LH is saturated or if it’s a model variant fallback issue?
- Priyom: collect latest telemetry and push redwood-telemetry-logs-0706.zip to the incident board.
- Rishi: I’ll draft a short exec note for LuminaLeadership and coordinate any credit/SLA exception asks.

I’m standing up a 10:30 PST (17:30 UTC) bridge; link will follow. If you can’t make that, send a 1–2 line status now.

Karthik
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike in 5xx + tokens delayed across /generate endpoint

Karthik — quick triage: initial telemetry shows their dedicated pool hitting sustained queue depth and several model workers are cycling due to OOM on longer sequences. Not a global control plane event.

Actions taken (ongoing):
- Enabled short-term burst capacity on LH’s pool to absorb traffic (will cost; we can roll back).
- Bumped model variant from v14-q4 to v14-q2 fallback (lower mem usage) for chat-long route to reduce OOMs.
- Priyom is exporting detailed worker logs; I’ll attach once available.

Preliminary ask for customer: confirm whether they can tolerate ~15–30s increased tail latency for long chats during the next hour while we stabilize, or whether they want us to provision additional reserved capacity/scale now.

Marissa

Attaching logs and quick analysis (uploaded to incident board): redwood-telemetry-logs-0706.zip — key points below:
- 07:38–07:52 PST: clear bump in KV cache misses for chat-long sessions (longer prefix).
- Several worker restarts correlated with peak memory pressure on the instance type (A100-40GB mixed workloads).
- Autoscaler attempted to add workers but hit a rate limit because this pool has a conservative scale policy.

Recommendation: keep burst on for 60 minutes, relax scale policy temporarily for this pool, and follow with a quota review for LH (they are near their commit). I will attach the log bundle to the Jira: INF-9453.

Priyom

1) Can Redwood provide a short executive summary we can share internally (1 paragraph + bullet summary + timeline)? Our legal/ops team is asking for an official note.

Subject: LuminaHealth — Executive summary & customer communication (final)

Team — sending the one-paragraph executive summary Sam asked for (copy to LuminaLeadership below). This is the official customer-facing note; please don’t share other internal commentary.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (customer-facing) — LuminaHealth incident 2026-07-06:
Between 07:38–07:52 PST we observed an elevated 5xx rate and throughput degradation for LuminaHealth’s dedicated pool servicing long-chat sessions. Root cause: memory pressure on select model workers causing OOM restarts in combination with a high KV cache miss rate for long-prefix requests. Immediate mitigations implemented: (1) temporary burst capacity to absorb excess traffic, (2) model-variant fallback to a lower-memory variant for long-chat routes, and (3) temporary relaxation of the pool’s scale policy to allow additional workers to come up. Impact: degraded throughput and increased tail latency for multi-turn chat users for approximately 30–45 minutes. Next steps: detailed runbook with configuration changes and a recommended commit adjustment (estimated +20% reserved capacity) delivered by 2026-07-08 17:00 UTC; customer follow-up review scheduled for 2026-07-09. We will prepare an SLA exception packet if LuminaHealth requests credits after review.

Please confirm and I will send to Samantha and Rajiv now.

Karthik
